column2: stop it from running at boot
column3: CLARIFY: Which service or autostart item should be disabled? Give me the name and I'll use 'systemctl disable' or remove the autostart entry.
CLARIFY: Which server (a process running on this machine, or a remote one), and which port or address? I'll check if the service is listening.
CLARIFY: For which service? Many support 'systemctl reload SERVICE_NAME' to reread config without restarting - tell me which one.
CLARIFY: Which service? Run 'systemctl --failed' to see crashed ones and share the name, or paste 'systemctl status NAME' so I can see the failure.
CLARIFY: Do you want all processes (ps aux), only those listening on a port (ss -tlnp), only systemd services (systemctl list-units), or a specific name?
CLARIFY: Which daemon is misbehaving? Share the name from 'systemctl list-units --type=service' or describe the symptom.
CLARIFY: Which worker process - a celery worker, a background job runner, a custom script? Give me a name or PID.
CLARIFY: Which application, and how is it running - as a systemd service (which one), under tmux/screen, via supervisor, in a Docker container?
CLARIFY: Zombie processes can't be killed directly - they need the parent to reap them. Run 'ps -A -ostat,ppid | grep -e '[zZ]'' to find the parent PID and we can act on that.
CLARIFY: Stop all running services (dangerous - would take the system offline), or just one service? Tell me what 'everything' means here.

CLARIFY: Which database (postgresql, mysql, mariadb, mongodb), and what does 'systemctl status DB_NAME' show? Paste the error.
CLARIFY: Is the web server running (systemctl status nginx OR apache2)? Or is the issue with the application behind it? Share the error you're seeing.
CLARIFY: What's the symptom - service not running, connection refused, or slow responses? Share 'systemctl status redis-server' and the client error.
CLARIFY: All Docker containers ('docker restart $(docker ps -q)'), only those in a specific docker-compose project, or only stopped ones?
CLARIFY: Which database, and do you know the query's PID? In Postgres: 'SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid);' - I need the database type and query identifier.
CLARIFY: Which cron job, and what's wrong with it? Run 'crontab -l' to see your jobs and share which line isn't working.
CLARIFY: Which scheduled task - a cron entry, a systemd timer, or an at-job? Share what you have and which to remove.
CLARIFY: Which cron entry do you want removed? Run 'crontab -l' and tell me which line - or share the command pattern.
CLARIFY: Which systemd timer? Run 'systemctl list-timers --all' and share the name. Or is it a cron job that's not firing?
CLARIFY: Which script do you want running in the background? Should it restart on failure (systemd) or just keep running until logout (nohup)?
CLARIFY: Which loop - a shell loop in a terminal (Ctrl+C), a background script (need PID), or an infinite job in a service? Tell me where it's running.
CLARIFY: Which app, and how is it managed (systemd, docker, supervisor)? Share 'journalctl -u SERVICE_NAME -n 50' so we can see why it's crashing.
CLARIFY: For which service - I need to edit its systemd unit (Restart= line). Tell me the service name.
CLARIFY: Which service should restart on failure? I'll add Restart=on-failure to its systemd unit - share the service name.
CLARIFY: Port 8080 is clear, but should I also kill the process, or just report what's there? 'sudo lsof -i :8080' will show it - want me to act?
CLARIFY: Which dev server (Node, Python, Rails, Webpack, Vite)? They run on different ports - is yours on 3000, 5173, 8000? Or share the process name.

column2: the service is in a bad state
column3: CLARIFY: Which service, and what state - failed, activating, deactivating? Run 'systemctl status SERVICE_NAME' and paste the output.
CLARIFY: What's spawning what? Share the process name (e.g., 'ps -ef --forest') so I can find the parent and stop it correctly.
CLARIFY: Which process? Try 'kill -9 PID' if a normal kill failed. If it's a zombie or D-state, we can't kill it - share 'ps -A -ostat,pid,cmd | grep PROCESS' so I see.
CLARIFY: Which service or process should I restart? 'Cleanly' implies graceful - I'll send SIGTERM first. Just tell me the name.

column2: the worker isnt picking up jobs
column3: CLARIFY: Which worker (celery, sidekiq, rq, custom) and what's the queue/broker (Redis, RabbitMQ)? Share recent worker logs so we can see what's happening.
CLARIFY: Which systemd unit? Run 'systemctl --failed' to find failed ones, or tell me the name and I'll check status.
CLARIFY: All print jobs (cancel -a), only on a specific printer, or a specific job ID? Run 'lpstat -o' to see job IDs.
CLARIFY: Restart the bluetooth service ('systemctl restart bluetooth'), or just toggle bluetooth (bluetoothctl power off/on)?
CLARIFY: Which interface is affected (run 'iw dev')? And do you want me to restart NetworkManager, or investigate the driver/logs first?
CLARIFY: Disable unattended-upgrades package, mask the systemd timer, or just delay updates? Each has different long-term implications.
CLARIFY: Always run meaning - on boot (systemd service), on a schedule (cron/timer), or restart whenever it crashes? And which script (path)?
CLARIFY: Apt dependency error - share the exact error message? Or do you mean a missing dependency for a different tool (npm, pip, etc.)?
CLARIFY: Stop which sync - rsync, Dropbox, Syncthing, OneDrive client, Google Drive client? Each has a different process name.
CLARIFY: Which daemon - share the service name? I'll check 'systemctl status NAME' and decide between restart and kill.
CLARIFY: All instances of which process? Run 'pgrep -lf KEYWORD' and confirm what comes up - I'll then use 'pkill' on the right name.
CLARIFY: You want to stop the cron daemon entirely (systemctl stop cron)? That would disable all scheduled jobs system-wide - is that intended?
CLARIFY: What's the symptom - nginx won't start, returns 502, or won't reload config? Share 'sudo nginx -t' output and 'systemctl status nginx'.
CLARIFY: Stop CUPS (systemctl stop cups), or only cancel current jobs (cancel -a)? Stopping the whole service disables printing until restart.
CLARIFY: Which build (make, cargo, npm, mvn, gradle), and what error appears? Share the last 30 lines of build output.
CLARIFY: Which program autostarts - check ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop for desktop apps, or it might be a systemd user service. Which one do you mean?
CLARIFY: That's 'sudo systemctl restart bluetooth' - confirm you want a full daemon restart, or just toggle the radio with 'bluetoothctl power off; bluetoothctl power on'?
CLARIFY: Which daemons do you consider unneeded? Run 'systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running' and tell me which to disable.
CLARIFY: All python processes you own (pkill -u $USER python)? That would also kill anything python-based you might need - confirm or be more specific?
CLARIFY: Stop them gracefully (let current tasks finish - 'celery control shutdown' on the right app) or kill immediately ('pkill -f celery')? And which celery app?
CLARIFY: Which queue - print queue (cups), mail queue (postfix), a job queue (sidekiq/rq/celery), or apt's package queue? Tell me which.
CLARIFY: Which script, and what should happen on failure - restart automatically (systemd service with Restart=always)? And which user should run it?
CLARIFY: Which timer (systemctl list-timers), and what's the misbehavior - firing too often, not firing, drifting? Share the timer name and journal output.
CLARIFY: Which sync service is auto-syncing - Syncthing, Nextcloud, Dropbox, Google Drive? I'll stop that specific one.
CLARIFY: Which service did you edit the config for? Often 'systemctl reload SERVICE' is enough - share the service name.
CLARIFY: Listening on which port, or all ports? 'ss -tlnp' shows all TCP listeners - do you want that, or filter to one port?

column2: stop the listener on the port
column3: CLARIFY: Which port number? I'll find what's listening with 'sudo lsof -i :PORT' and then stop that process.
CLARIFY: Of which service or process? Many services have specific graceful-stop commands (nginx -s quit, postgres pg_ctl stop -m smart). Tell me which.
CLARIFY: Which sync - share the tool's name? I want to make sure I stop the right one and don't interrupt other syncs you might be running.
CLARIFY: For which service - I'd need to edit its config or pass a flag. Tell me the service and what kind of debug output you need.
CLARIFY: Kill all processes belonging to which user (e.g., 'pkill -KILL -u USERNAME')? Confirm the username and that you want all of them killed.
CLARIFY: Just the running ones ('docker stop $(docker ps -q)'), or also remove stopped ones? And should this include containers from compose projects?
CLARIFY: What's the symptom - snaps won't install, daemon is failing, refreshing forever? Share 'systemctl status snapd' and the snap command output.
CLARIFY: For which service - I'll add Restart=on-failure to its systemd unit. Tell me the service name and how many retries you want.
CLARIFY: Graceful stop (apache2ctl graceful-stop - lets connections finish) or fast stop (systemctl stop apache2)? Confirm.
CLARIFY: Which API process - share name or PID? Then I can profile (strace, perf), check resource limits, or restart if appropriate.
CLARIFY: Which service do you want to check? Tell me the name and I'll run 'systemctl is-active' on it.
CLARIFY: Restart which service or the whole system, every night, only tonight, or once a week? I'll set up a cron or systemd timer.
CLARIFY: Which service or script? I'll wrap it in a systemd unit with Restart=always - share the name and the command to start it.
CLARIFY: Which user systemd service (systemctl --user list-units shows them)? Give me the name.
CLARIFY: All jobs in this shell (kill $(jobs -p)), or all background processes owned by you (pkill -u $USER)? The second is much broader.
CLARIFY: What symptom - frozen, missing icons, won't start? On X11 you can restart with Alt+F2 then 'r'. On Wayland you need to log out. Which session are you in?
CLARIFY: Which game (process name)? Run 'ps -ef | grep -i game_keyword' and share what appears - I'll kill the right PID.
CLARIFY: Restart NetworkManager (desktop, common case), systemd-networkd (servers), or just bounce a specific interface (ip link set down/up)?
CLARIFY: PulseAudio (systemctl --user stop pulseaudio.socket pulseaudio.service) or PipeWire (systemctl --user stop pipewire)? Run 'pactl info' to see which is in use.
CLARIFY: That's 'sudo systemctl restart bluetooth' - confirm you want the system-wide bluetooth daemon restarted, not just toggling the radio?
CLARIFY: Run 'ps aux --sort=-pcpu | head -5' and tell me which process - or share what's at the top so I act on the correct one.
CLARIFY: What's freezing - one app (which one), the whole desktop, or a server? For a single app, kill it; for the whole system, the diagnostic is different.
CLARIFY: Which script (give me the name from 'ps aux | grep SCRIPT_NAME')? I'll kill that PID once we identify the right one.
CLARIFY: Which container (docker ps to list)? Use 'docker restart NAME' or 'docker compose restart SERVICE' depending on how it was launched.
CLARIFY: On a real cluster node? What's the symptom - share 'systemctl status kubelet' and 'journalctl -u kubelet -n 100'. I'll triage from there.

column2: make the daemon reload its file
column3: CLARIFY: Which daemon and which config file? Most reload with 'systemctl reload SERVICE' or by sending SIGHUP - tell me the service.
CLARIFY: Orphaned processes are reparented to init - they're usually fine. Which process are you concerned about? Share PID or name.
CLARIFY: Which indexer - tracker (GNOME), baloo (KDE), or an app's search index? Tell me which.
CLARIFY: Restart Docker daemon if it crashes (it already does via systemd), or restart a specific container on host reboot (--restart=always)? Which?
CLARIFY: Access to what (a file, folder, service)? And for which user, and which level (read-only, read/write, full ownership)?
CLARIFY: For which file or folder, and to what - readable by everyone, executable, restricted to owner? Tell me the path and desired access.
CLARIFY: What username, should they have sudo access, a regular shell or be a service account, and which groups should they belong to?
CLARIFY: For which file or folder, and which user/group should own it? Run 'ls -l PATH' so we see what it is now.
CLARIFY: Which files or folder, and what's her username on this system? I'd also need to decide between adding her to a group or using ACLs.

column2: make this folder open to everyone
column3: CLARIFY: Read-only for everyone (chmod 755) or read/write (chmod 775 with group, or 777 - which is risky)? Which folder?
CLARIFY: Whose access, and to what - a file, a folder, a database, ssh access? Tell me the user and the resource.
CLARIFY: What's the username, and should they have unrestricted sudo (in the sudo group) or only specific commands (via /etc/sudoers.d)?
CLARIFY: Which account, and lock how - prevent password login (passwd -l), disable shell, or fully expire the account?
CLARIFY: Which username, and should I keep or remove their home directory and mailspool? Use 'userdel' vs 'userdel -r'.
CLARIFY: Which file (give me the path)? Executable for owner only (chmod u+x), or for everyone (chmod +x)?
CLARIFY: Which command or file gave the permission denied error? Paste the full message and I'll figure out what permission needs adjusting.
CLARIFY: Which group, to which file or folder, and what kind of access (read, read+write, read+write+execute)?
CLARIFY: For which file or directory, and to which user? Should I also change the group, and apply recursively?
CLARIFY: Which group (docker, sudo, www-data, dialout, etc.)? You may need to log out and back in for group membership to take effect.
CLARIFY: Username for the service account, should it have a shell (no, usually /usr/sbin/nologin), and what home directory if any?

column2: let it write to this folder
column3: CLARIFY: Let which process or user write to which folder? I need both to set the right ownership or ACL.
CLARIFY: For which user, and for ALL commands or only specific ones (much safer - which commands)? NOPASSWD on everything is high-risk.
CLARIFY: What username should I create, and do you have his public SSH key (where, or paste it)? Should he have sudo?
CLARIFY: Which user, and from which group? Also, do you want them in any other groups - 'gpasswd -d USER GROUP' removes from one specific group.
CLARIFY: Which file - and what user should own it? Current owner might be 'root' or another user; run 'ls -l PATH' so we can see.
CLARIFY: Which file or folder? Read-only for owner too (chmod 444 / chattr +i), or just for others (chmod 644)?
CLARIFY: For which user, and what policy - expire in N days, force change on next login, lock if not changed?
CLARIFY: Switch this user to SSH-key-only login (passwd -l)? Or remove the user's password entirely? These are different.
CLARIFY: Which database (postgres, mysql), which user inside the DB, to which database/tables, and which permissions (SELECT, INSERT, ALL)?

column2: let the web server read my files
column3: CLARIFY: Which web server (nginx, apache - they run as www-data), which files, and read-only? I'll set group permissions or ACLs.
CLARIFY: Private from whom - other local users (chmod 700), or specific user/group? Which folder?
CLARIFY: Share what (folder), with which users, and how - filesystem permissions (need a shared group), Samba, NFS, or a cloud-style sync?

column2: let everyone in this group write
column3: CLARIFY: Which group, to which folder, and should new files inherit group ownership (setgid)? If yes I'll also chmod g+s the folder.
CLARIFY: From a specific file/folder, or recursively across a tree (e.g., your home directory)? I'd use 'chmod -R o-w PATH'.
CLARIFY: For which file or folder, and which users/groups should have which access? ACLs let you grant per-user rights beyond owner/group/other.

column2: make the script runnable by everyone
column3: CLARIFY: Which script - and confirm it's safe to expose to all users on this system? Path and confirmation, please.
CLARIFY: Disable root password login (passwd -l root)? Note this still allows sudo from authorized users - is that what you want?
CLARIFY: Add the jenkins user to the docker group? That effectively grants root - confirm. Run 'usermod -aG docker jenkins' if so.
CLARIFY: Whose home folder, and accessible by whom? Granting access to a home folder can expose private data - what's the use case?
CLARIFY: Which user, and how - lock their password (passwd -l) so they can't log in but data is preserved, or expire the account?

column2: give read access to log files
column3: CLARIFY: For which user, and which log files? Many require root or adm group - I can add the user to 'adm' if that's appropriate.

column2: make a folder writable by apache
column3: CLARIFY: Which folder, and should apache (www-data) be the owner, in the owning group, or via ACL? Recursive?
CLARIFY: Of which file or folder, from whom to whom, recursively (chown -R)? Also confirm with 'ls -l' so I see current state.
CLARIFY: Default for what - home directories (700), system files (644 for files / 755 for dirs)? Which path needs reset?

column2: let me write to var www
column3: CLARIFY: Add your user to the www-data group and chmod g+w the folder, or chown it to you? Which is preferred depends on if a server also writes there.

column2: make the script owned by root
column3: CLARIFY: Which script, and should it also be setuid (runs with root regardless of who launches)? Setuid is risky - confirm if so.

column2: set up shared folder for the family
column3: CLARIFY: A local-disk shared folder (which users), or a network share via Samba so other devices can connect? Either works.
CLARIFY: Which user (now deleted), and where do their files live - /home/USER, plus any orphaned files elsewhere? Identify with 'find / -nouser'.
CLARIFY: Which user, and via what - local login (set shell with chsh) or SSH (add public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys)?
CLARIFY: Which user, and disable how - set shell to /usr/sbin/nologin (login fails politely) or /bin/false (login fails silently)?

column2: give the user a strong password
column3: CLARIFY: Which user, and should I generate a random password (and how should you receive it), or do you want to set one manually?

column2: make the file private to me
column3: CLARIFY: Which file - I'll chmod 600 if it's a regular file, 700 if directory. Confirm path.
CLARIFY: Which file, with which local user? Either chmod o+r (anyone on system reads), or use ACLs to grant just that user.
CLARIFY: A guest user for local login, or guest access to a Samba/file share? Each setup is different.

column2: block a user from logging in
column3: CLARIFY: Which user, and how - lock password (passwd -l), set shell to nologin, or remove from ssh allow list? Each blocks a different login path.
CLARIFY: Read access to which file or folder? On a multi-user system, chmod o+r exposes it to all local users - confirm path.
CLARIFY: Which file or folder, and what should they be (e.g., 644 for files / 755 for directories, or stricter 600/700)?

column2: make sure no one else can read this
column3: CLARIFY: Which file - and 'no one else' meaning no other local user? I'll chmod 600 and confirm ownership belongs to you.

column2: give the dev team access to the deploy folder
column3: CLARIFY: Are 'devs' a unix group already (run 'getent group devs')? If not, what users should be in it, and which folder needs write access?

column2: set up file sharing for the office
column3: CLARIFY: Local network (Samba/CIFS for Windows interop, NFS for Linux/Mac), or cloud-like (Nextcloud)? Which folder shared, and to which users?

column2: let the user mount usb sticks
column3: CLARIFY: Add the user to the 'plugdev' group (works on Ubuntu desktop), or do you need them to mount manually via sudo? Different paths.

column2: the file says i dont have permission
column3: CLARIFY: Which file (full path), and what are you trying to do (read, write, execute)? Share 'ls -l PATH' so I know the current permissions.
CLARIFY: Everywhere on your home folder (chown -R you:you ~), or system-wide (very risky)? Tell me the scope; system-wide can break the OS.
CLARIFY: Which files (e.g., ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, a credentials folder)? I'll chmod 600/700 - confirm the paths.

column2: give docker access to that folder
column3: CLARIFY: Docker containers run as whatever user the image uses. Which folder, mounted into which container, and what UID:GID does the container's process use?
CLARIFY: For which kubeconfig (path), and what's failing - 'permission denied' for the file (chmod 600 ~/.kube/config), or RBAC denial in the cluster?
CLARIFY: Which log directory? I'll either chown to www-data or add ACL so www-data can write. Confirm the path.
CLARIFY: For which user(s), and to what - force password change on next login (chage -d 0 USER), or set a policy for expiry every N days?
CLARIFY: Restricted how - no shell (rsync/sftp-only), no sudo, chrooted, limited resources (cgroups)? Tell me what they should and shouldn't do.
CLARIFY: For which user - I'd create a chrooted sftp-only account, or restrict to specific commands. Tell me the username and what they need to access.
CLARIFY: Where is 'here' - the current directory? Run 'pwd' and 'ls -l' so I see the path and current ownership before chmod or chown.
CLARIFY: Strip world-writable from a single file/folder, or scan a tree to find and fix all of them (find PATH -perm -o=w)?
CLARIFY: Whose home folder, and to what - 700 (private, most common), 750 (private to user, readable by their group), or 755 (world-readable)?

column2: let me run sudo without prompting all the time
column3: CLARIFY: For your user, for which commands? NOPASSWD for everything is risky; safer is for specific commands. List the commands you want.
CLARIFY: Read-only of what - filesystem (limit via filesystem ACLs), a database (specific DB grants), or a Git repo? Each is a different setup.
CLARIFY: Share what (file or folder), with all local users on this system? I'll chmod accordingly - what's the path?
CLARIFY: Which config file - e.g., ~/.ssh/config, ~/.aws/credentials, an app config? I'll set 600 or 700 once I have the path.
CLARIFY: Audit what - find world-writable files, find SUID binaries, files with no owner? Tell me which class of risky permission to scan for.
CLARIFY: Swap how - rename a user (usermod -l NEW OLD), change UID, or change who owns home files? Tell me what 'swap' means.
CLARIFY: For which user, and to what value (022 for default permissive, 027 for restrict-other, 077 for owner-only)? And system-wide or just your shell?

column2: let only members of a group write
column3: CLARIFY: Which group, which folder, and should new files inherit the group (setgid)? Need group name and path.

column2: make read writable for all in my project
column3: CLARIFY: Which folder, who is 'all in my project' (a unix group - which one)? I'll set group ownership and chmod 775.
CLARIFY: Which user, to which file or folder? I'll use ACLs (setfacl -m u:USER:rwx PATH) since standard perms only have one owner.
CLARIFY: Remove which user from the sudo (or wheel) group? Or remove a specific NOPASSWD line from sudoers? Tell me what they currently have.
CLARIFY: Pull access to what - a Git repo on this server, a Docker registry, an apt mirror, a network share? Each is set up differently.
CLARIFY: Add additional user accounts (how many, what usernames), or set up authentication for an existing service (like SSH for multiple keys)? Be specific.
CLARIFY: For which user(s), on which filesystem, and what limit (size in MB/GB, inode count, or both)? Quotas need quota tools and fstab options.
CLARIFY: 'This' meaning which file or folder, and what should the permissions be? Share the path and intended mode (e.g., 644 / 755 / 600).
CLARIFY: Add to sudo group for general admin, or specific groups for specific access (docker, libvirt, dialout)? What do you actually need to do?
CLARIFY: For which folder, and to which user/group? Confirm the path - 'chown -R USER:GROUP PATH' is the form.
CLARIFY: Which service account, to which resource (file, folder, port, system call), and what level of access? Be specific so I can keep privileges minimal.
CLARIFY: Add your user to the docker group? Be aware this grants effective root via container mounts - confirm if you accept that risk.

column2: make a folder for everyone in our group
column3: CLARIFY: Which group, and where should the folder live? I'll mkdir, chown root:GROUP, chmod 2775 so new files inherit the group.
CLARIFY: Lock the screen now (loginctl lock-session), set an auto-lock timeout, or harden filesystem permissions? Different actions for each goal.
CLARIFY: ~/.ssh should be 700, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys 600, private keys 600. Which file is misbehaving, or do you want the standard set applied?

column2: change file permissions to safe defaults
column3: CLARIFY: For which directory tree, and what's 'safe' to you - 644/755 (default), 640/750 (group-only), or 600/700 (owner-only)?
CLARIFY: Push access to what - a Git remote (need ssh key in remote), Docker registry (need creds), package repo? Tell me the destination.
CLARIFY: For which file - make it executable (chmod +x PATH)? Or for a folder of scripts, all matching a pattern?

column2: let me see other users home folders
column3: CLARIFY: This usually requires sudo and revealing private data. What's the actual goal - administering a specific user's files, or browsing? I might suggest a safer approach.
CLARIFY: For which user, and is the ftp server already running (which one - vsftpd, proftpd)? Or do you want SFTP via SSH instead (more secure)?
CLARIFY: Kill their active sessions (pkill -KILL -u USER), lock the account, or fully delete them? Each is different in severity.
CLARIFY: Which folder, and is the postgres user named 'postgres'? I'll chown or use ACLs - confirm the path.
CLARIFY: For which user, allowing which commands? I'll write a file in /etc/sudoers.d/ - share the username and the commands they should be allowed to run.

column2: let two users edit the same file
column3: CLARIFY: Create a shared group, chown the file to that group, chmod g+w? Tell me the file path and the two usernames.
CLARIFY: Which disk is running low (run 'df -h')? And what should I target - apt cache, old kernels, large files in home, browser caches?
CLARIFY: Look at which mount point (home, root, an external drive)? I'll run du or ncdu - tell me the path you want analyzed.
CLARIFY: Which drive (run 'lsblk' to see), and where should it be mounted (e.g., /mnt/usb, /media/$USER/data)?
CLARIFY: Which device (run 'lsblk'), and to which filesystem (ext4 for Linux, exFAT for cross-platform, NTFS for Windows)? Formatting destroys all data on it.
CLARIFY: Which partition (lsblk to identify), and to what size? Is there free unallocated space after it, or do you need to shrink a neighbor first?
CLARIFY: Across all mounts ('df -h') or breakdown by folder ('du -sh /path/*')? Which path if du?
CLARIFY: What kind of share - NFS, Samba (CIFS), SSHFS? And what's the server address, share name, and mount point on this machine?
CLARIFY: Which mount? Run 'mount | grep -v ^proc' to list, then tell me the mount point or device.
CLARIFY: Where to look (home folder, /var, the whole system), and how big counts as big (>100MB, >1GB)? Sort by size descending?
CLARIFY: Starting from which directory, and how deep to traverse? I'll run 'du -h --max-depth=N PATH | sort -h' - need both inputs.
CLARIFY: How big a swapfile (e.g., 4G, 8G), and where to place it (default /swapfile)? Or do you want a swap partition instead?
CLARIFY: Resize the existing /swapfile or create an additional one? And to what size? Current size: check with 'swapon --show'.
CLARIFY: For which drive (lsblk to identify), and do you want a quick check (smartctl -H) or a long self-test (smartctl -t long)?
CLARIFY: What's the symptom - filesystem errors, can't mount, slow performance? And which device/partition? Different fixes for each.
CLARIFY: For all disks (lsblk) or a specific one (lsblk /dev/sda)? And do you want partition table type too (fdisk -l)?
CLARIFY: Add a new disk (which device), expand an existing partition (which), or extend a logical volume (LVM)? Tell me your storage layout.
CLARIFY: Which type of cleanup - apt cache, old kernels, journal logs, Docker images, large files in home? Each has its own command.
CLARIFY: Which mount point is filling (df -h shows this), and from which directory should I search for the culprits (e.g., /var, ~)?
CLARIFY: Which RAID level (0, 1, 5, 10), using which devices (lsblk), and via what (mdadm software RAID, ZFS, btrfs)? This destroys data on the devices.
CLARIFY: Which ISO file, and which USB device (lsblk)? I'll use dd - this destroys all data on the USB.
CLARIFY: Which drive? Run 'sudo smartctl -a /dev/sdX' on the device you suspect - tell me which, and I'll interpret the output.

column2: show me whats on the disk
column3: CLARIFY: A directory tree (which path), partitions (lsblk), or filesystem usage breakdown (du)? Each gives a different view.
CLARIFY: Which partition, and what's the new size? Also: is the filesystem unmounted? Shrinking a mounted filesystem is unsafe.
CLARIFY: Where to search, and what's the size threshold (>100MB, >500MB) and age threshold (older than 30 days, 90 days)?
CLARIFY: Look in your home folder, the root filesystem, or a specific path? I'll run 'du -sh PATH/* | sort -h' once we agree on the path.
CLARIFY: Where to search, and what's 'biggest' - top 10 by size, or files over a threshold? Also confirm: review before deleting, or auto-delete?
CLARIFY: Which device (run 'sudo fdisk -l' to see NTFS partitions), and to which mount point (e.g., /mnt/windows)? Read-only or read-write?
CLARIFY: Which logical volume (lvs), and by how much (e.g., +10G or to a specific size)? Plus resize the filesystem on top?
CLARIFY: A LVM snapshot of a logical volume (which one), a btrfs snapshot (which subvolume), or a ZFS snapshot? Tell me which storage system.
CLARIFY: What to back up (which folder), and which external drive (lsblk, what's the mount point)? Tool - rsync, tar, or restic?

CLARIFY: On which disk (lsblk), how big, what type/filesystem, and where in the disk? Also: is there free space?
CLARIFY: Which partition (lsblk to identify exact name like /dev/sda3)? Deleting destroys data on it - confirm.

CLARIFY: Which device, and what's the symptom - won't mount, errors in dmesg, files unreadable? I'll run fsck or smartctl, but I need to know which.
CLARIFY: To grow the root partition, the disk must have unallocated space after it (or be on LVM). Run 'lsblk' and 'sudo parted -l' so we can see the layout.
CLARIFY: Look in /var/log (rotate or clear logs), /var/cache (apt clean), /var/lib/docker, or somewhere else? Run 'du -sh /var/* | sort -h' to find the biggest.

column2: see who is using a mount
column3: CLARIFY: Which mount point? I'll run 'fuser -mv MOUNTPOINT' or 'lsof MOUNTPOINT' to show processes holding files - tell me the path.
CLARIFY: Which drive, and do you want to mark them and continue (badblocks + mkfs with -l), or replace the drive? Sharing 'smartctl -a /dev/sdX' would help triage.
CLARIFY: Source and destination devices? I'll use 'dd' or 'partclone' - confirm both, and that the destination is empty (data will be overwritten).
CLARIFY: Which partition is /boot ('df /boot'), and where should the backup go? I'll dd it to an image file or another disk.
CLARIFY: Create a new subvolume (where on a btrfs mount, and what name)? Or list/manage existing ones? Tell me the goal.
CLARIFY: Run fstrim now on all mounts ('sudo fstrim -av'), enable the weekly fstrim timer ('systemctl enable fstrim.timer'), or just one mount?
CLARIFY: /boot is filling with old kernels. Remove unused kernels with 'sudo apt autoremove --purge', or do you also want to clean initramfs caches?
CLARIFY: Identify what's writing (iotop) so we can stop the culprit? Or are you trying to spin down an idle drive (hdparm -y)?
CLARIFY: Tune mount options (noatime), upgrade hardware, switch scheduler? What's your bottleneck - random reads, sequential writes, latency?

column2: what files have i changed today
column3: CLARIFY: In which directory should I search? I'll run 'find PATH -mtime -1 -type f' once you confirm the starting path.

column2: find files modified in the last hour
column3: CLARIFY: In which directory tree? 'find PATH -mmin -60 -type f' - tell me PATH.
CLARIFY: Which folder, and how many to show? E.g., 'ls -lt FOLDER | tail -20' for the 20 oldest by mtime.
CLARIFY: Btrfs rebalance (which mount), ZFS rebalance, or moving files between disks manually? Tell me the storage tech in use.
CLARIFY: In which directory? 'find PATH -type f -printf %S\t%p\n' shows sparseness - tell me where to look.
CLARIFY: Run 'nix-collect-garbage' (current user) or '-d' (delete old generations system-wide, requires root)? Also: how many generations to keep?
CLARIFY: Remove old snap revisions ('snap list --all' to see), or remove unused snaps entirely? Snaps keep 3 revisions by default - reduce to how many?
CLARIFY: Remove dangling images (docker image prune), all unused images (-a), stopped containers, unused volumes, or everything (docker system prune -a --volumes)?
CLARIFY: Limit by size ('journalctl --vacuum-size=200M') or by age ('journalctl --vacuum-time=2weeks')? Pick a target.
CLARIFY: Truncate /var/log/kern.log, or vacuum journalctl (which stores kernel messages)? And what's the goal - free space or hide info?
CLARIFY: For which user, on which filesystem, and what limit (soft, hard, in MB or GB, plus inode limit)? Quotas need to be enabled in fstab first.
CLARIFY: Which partition, and to what new size? Filesystem must be unmounted, and shrinking carries risk - confirm a backup is in place.
CLARIFY: Source (/home is on which disk?) and destination drive (lsblk)? I'll set up the new partition, rsync data, and update /etc/fstab.
CLARIFY: For which disk (lsblk)? This affects bootability - is the system currently booting from this disk? And do you have a backup?
CLARIFY: All partitions ('blkid' or 'lsblk -o NAME,UUID,LABEL'), or just one device (blkid /dev/sdX)? Either works.
CLARIFY: Which partition (lsblk), and what label? Tool depends on filesystem - e2label for ext, ntfslabel for NTFS, exfatlabel for exFAT.
CLARIFY: Which filesystem (device path)? It must be unmounted for fsck. Boot to recovery, or unmount it now? Which mount?
CLARIFY: What's the current slow part - kernel init, services, GUI loading? Run 'systemd-analyze blame' and share the top entries.
CLARIFY: Which images need compacting - removing layers, multistage build to slim, or just pruning unused? Share the image name(s) and goal.
CLARIFY: Docker volumes ('docker volume prune'), LVM volumes (which to remove from 'lvs'), or libvirt storage volumes? Different tools.
CLARIFY: From which directory? I'll run 'find PATH -type f -size +1G' once you confirm the path.
CLARIFY: Where to place the swapfile (default /swapfile)? I'll dd or fallocate 8G, mkswap, swapon, and add to fstab - confirm.
CLARIFY: Disable swap entirely (swapoff -a, remove from fstab), or only one specific swap (which - 'swapon --show')?
CLARIFY: For which device (lsblk)? I'll run 'sudo smartctl -A /dev/sdX' and interpret the Wear_Leveling and Total_LBAs_Written attributes.
CLARIFY: Which mount, and disk hog by space (du) or by I/O (iotop)? Each addresses a different problem - which?
CLARIFY: Resize the root filesystem - this is non-trivial and usually needs offline (rescue) tools unless on LVM/btrfs. What's the storage layout? Backup in place?
CLARIFY: Sequential read benchmark ('sudo hdparm -tT /dev/sdX'), random IO ('fio'), or just casual ('dd if=/dev/sdX of=/dev/null bs=1M count=1024')? Which device?
CLARIFY: For which device (lsblk), and which scheduler (none for NVMe SSD, mq-deadline for SATA SSD, bfq for desktops)? I'll write to /sys/block/.../queue/scheduler.
CLARIFY: How old (older than 30 days, 90 days), and any file types to skip (e.g., keep recent .pdf invoices)? Default is everything in ~/Downloads.
CLARIFY: This needs two steps: resize the disk in the hypervisor (which - VirtualBox, VMware, qemu, cloud?), then expand inside the VM. Which hypervisor?
CLARIFY: Which file? Note: on SSDs, secure delete is mostly ineffective without full-device blkdiscard. On HDD I can use 'shred -u'. Tell me the file.
CLARIFY: From which directory? I'll run 'find PATH -xdev -type f -printf %h\n | sort | uniq -c | sort -n' to find folders with most files.
CLARIFY: For which mount/device - I can set noatime in fstab, ensure fstrim.timer is enabled, and pick a suitable scheduler. Confirm device.
CLARIFY: One mount remount ro, or set hardware switch? Which mount point? Note: forcing root rw->ro requires care - confirm which filesystem.
CLARIFY: All block devices (lsblk - includes mounted ones), or only USB devices (lsusb)? Each shows different info.
CLARIFY: On which path or device? Sequential write test - 'dd if=/dev/zero of=PATH/testfile bs=1M count=1024 conv=fdatasync'. Tell me where to write.
CLARIFY: What's the symptom - no connection, slow, DNS not resolving, specific site unreachable? And on which interface (run 'ip a')?
CLARIFY: Which port number, which protocol (TCP or UDP), and via which firewall (ufw, firewalld, iptables)? Also, restricted to which source IPs?
CLARIFY: From which source (IP, subnet, anywhere) to which port and service? I'll add the firewall rule once those are clear.
CLARIFY: Block which source IP, port, or protocol - and in which direction (incoming, outgoing)? Which firewall (ufw, firewalld, iptables)?
CLARIFY: External port -> internal IP:port? Also: forwarding via iptables on this host, or on a router? I'd need both endpoints.
CLARIFY: Internet speed (speedtest-cli), local LAN speed (iperf3 to another machine), or a specific connection? Tell me what to measure.
CLARIFY: What's wrong - won't connect, slow, drops repeatedly, no networks visible? And which interface (iw dev)?
CLARIFY: Local IP on your network (run 'ip -4 addr show' or 'hostname -I'), or public IP as seen by the internet ('curl ifconfig.me')?
CLARIFY: To where - a specific host (ping HOST), the internet at large (ping 8.8.8.8), or a specific port (nc -zv HOST PORT)?

CLARIFY: On which host or subnet, and which ports (default 1000, all 65535, or a list)? Scanning hosts you don't own may be against terms of service.
CLARIFY: For incoming traffic to this machine - via iptables on the same host, or upstream? Confirm direction and interface.
CLARIFY: Which source IP, and which firewall (ufw allow from IP to any port 22; firewall-cmd; raw iptables)? Plus current rules - share if any.
CLARIFY: Block all incoming (default deny), or also outgoing? And leaving SSH open so you don't lock yourself out? Be very careful on remote hosts.
CLARIFY: System-wide DNS resolver (edit /etc/resolv.conf or systemd-resolved), or for a single interface (NetworkManager / netplan)? Which servers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8)?
CLARIFY: What's failing - 'cannot resolve hostname' for everything or specific domains? Share an example: 'nslookup example.com' output, and which resolver you use.
CLARIFY: Real-time per-process (nethogs), per-interface aggregate (vnstat or 'ip -s link'), or per-connection (iftop)? Which is more useful?

CLARIFY: For which interface (ip link), what IP/netmask, gateway, and DNS? Plus configuration method - netplan (Ubuntu server), NetworkManager (desktop)?
CLARIFY: Which VPN - WireGuard, OpenVPN, IPsec? Do you have config from a provider, or are you setting up your own server? Either changes the steps.
CLARIFY: For which user/all users, via what - /etc/hosts (simple, defeated by VPN), iptables, or DNS-level (e.g., Pi-hole)? Which domain?
CLARIFY: SSH sessions (who, w), all network connections (ss -tunap), or LAN devices (nmap -sn SUBNET)? Each shows different info.

CLARIFY: Live packet capture (tcpdump - on which interface and filter?), or summary stats (vnstat -i INTERFACE)? Which interface from 'ip link'?
CLARIFY: What hostname, and apply where - 'hostnamectl set-hostname NEW' updates it. Also update /etc/hosts? Confirm the desired name.
CLARIFY: ICMP reachability (ping 8.8.8.8), DNS resolution (nslookup example.com), or HTTP fetch (curl -I https://example.com)? Or all three?
CLARIFY: As a client (do you have a config from a provider?) or a server (which port, peer count, network subnet)?

column3: CLARIFY: Which folder, and via what protocol - Samba (for Windows interop), NFS (Unix-friendly), SFTP (over SSH)? Plus which users/hosts should access?
