CLARIFY: Recent ones ('sudo grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log | tail -50') or via journalctl ('sudo journalctl -u ssh | grep -i fail')? Confirm range.
CLARIFY: Today at 3pm? I'll use 'journalctl --since="15:00" --until="15:30"' - confirm the time window and any service filter.
CLARIFY: In dmesg ('dmesg | grep -i -E "error|fail|i/o"') or SMART logs ('sudo smartctl -l error /dev/sdX')? Which device if SMART?
CLARIFY: For which service - I'd edit its config to redirect output, or use systemd's StandardOutput=file:/path. Tell me the service and target file.
CLARIFY: I'll search dmesg / journal: 'dmesg | grep -i oom' and 'journalctl | grep -i "killed process"'. Confirm window (current boot, all time).
CLARIFY: Force a logrotate run ('sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf'), or for one specific service? Confirm the scope.

column2: see what app wrote to log
column3: CLARIFY: Which log file, and what app? Often the log has the program in the syslog tag. Share a few lines or the path - we'll go from there.
CLARIFY: Cap journal usage (SystemMaxUse in journald.conf), set up logrotate for app logs (which app?), or both? What's the current usage ('journalctl --disk-usage')?
CLARIFY: Which service? Run 'journalctl -fu SERVICE_NAME' - share the unit name.
CLARIFY: Which user, and which journal scope? 'journalctl _UID=$(id -u USER)' shows that user's processes. Confirm username.

column2: see what changed in the system
column3: CLARIFY: Recent apt install/upgrade ('grep -i install /var/log/apt/history.log'), or files changed ('find PATH -mtime -1')? Different views.
CLARIFY: When did the slowness start? I'll look at journal around that time, check load ('uptime'), I/O ('iostat'), or CPU ('top'). Tell me when and which subsystem feels slow.
CLARIFY: All errors during current boot ('journalctl -b -p err'), or for the last boot ('journalctl -b -1 -p err')?

column2: see what services failed last boot
column3: CLARIFY: Failed during current boot ('systemctl --failed') or in the previous boot ('journalctl -b -1 -p err -u "*"')?
CLARIFY: Last error from which scope - journal ('journalctl -p err -n 1'), a specific service ('journalctl -u NAME -p err -n 1'), or a file?
CLARIFY: Bash history is already kept (~/.bash_history). Do you want richer logging - timestamps (HISTTIMEFORMAT), auditd, or 'script' to record a session?
CLARIFY: All entries ('journalctl' - lots), recent ('journalctl -n 200'), or by service/priority? Tell me what you're looking for.
CLARIFY: All system logs from yesterday ('journalctl --since yesterday --until today'), or one service ('journalctl -u SERVICE --since yesterday')?
CLARIFY: System-wide critical and above ('journalctl -p crit'), or just one service? Plus time range (recent, today, current boot)?
CLARIFY: Which errors - system journal critical ('journalctl -p err -b > /tmp/errors.txt'), or a specific app's log? Confirm source and destination.
CLARIFY: Which file path? I'll use 'tail -f FILE'. If it might rotate, prefer 'tail -F FILE' to follow renames.
CLARIFY: Which unit (service name)? 'journalctl -u UNIT' - tell me the unit name (you can list with 'systemctl list-units').
CLARIFY: Just 'history' shows your shell history. Want all entries, last N, or grep for a keyword? E.g., 'history | grep KEYWORD'.
CLARIFY: What keyword? I'll run 'history | grep KEYWORD' - tell me the keyword.
CLARIFY: In journal ('journalctl -p err'), in a specific log file (which path), or via grep across /var/log (be careful, large)?
CLARIFY: From which application or script? In bash you can use 'logger MESSAGE' to send to syslog. Tell me the source.
CLARIFY: From coredumps ('coredumpctl list'), or from journal entries with SIGSEGV ('journalctl | grep -i segfault')? Which scope?
CLARIFY: Reduce log verbosity for a service (which one?) or reduce overall journal storage? Each has a different mechanism.
CLARIFY: System-wide ('journalctl -p warning'), or just current boot ('journalctl -b -p warning')? Or one service?
CLARIFY: 'Events' meaning - journal entries, audit events (auditd), or specific app events? Tell me which event source.
CLARIFY: For which service or file? I can suggest reducing log_level in the service's config - tell me which.
CLARIFY: Recent auth events ('sudo journalctl -u sshd' or 'sudo cat /var/log/auth.log'), failed only ('lastb'), or successful ('last')?
CLARIFY: Current boot ('journalctl -b') or previous boot ('journalctl -b -1')? And the whole thing, just errors, or one service?
CLARIFY: Which service is failing? Share 'systemctl status SERVICE' and 'journalctl -u SERVICE -n 100' so I can see the actual error.
CLARIFY: Which warning, where? Sharing the exact text or which service would let me narrow the search via 'journalctl | grep'.
CLARIFY: For your current shell session, 'script /tmp/session.log' records everything. For system-wide, you'd need auditd or to bump journal verbosity. Which is the goal?

column2: find what wrote this log entry
column3: CLARIFY: Paste a sample log line so I can identify the unit/process. The journal records the source (_COMM, _SYSTEMD_UNIT) - I can match it.
CLARIFY: For which service - nginx (/var/log/nginx/access.log), apache (/var/log/apache2/access.log), or another? And what filter (errors only, specific IP)?

column2: see what gets logged on shutdown
column3: CLARIFY: Last boot's shutdown messages ('journalctl -b -1 -e' shows end of previous boot), or live capture next time you shutdown ('journalctl -f' before halt)?
CLARIFY: Which database (postgres /var/log/postgresql, mysql /var/log/mysql, mongodb /var/log/mongodb)? And by error pattern - connection refused, syntax, timeout?
CLARIFY: 'journalctl -b -1' shows the previous boot's full log; '-e' jumps to the end (last events before that reboot). Confirm you want the prior boot.
CLARIFY: 'journalctl --vacuum-time=1s' wipes nearly everything - confirm you want that, or do you want to keep a specific window (e.g., last day)?
CLARIFY: From auditd (if installed), AppArmor denials ('journalctl | grep apparmor'), SELinux (if enforcing), or PAM auth events? Which kind?
CLARIFY: All journal entries ('journalctl --since=-1h'), or a specific service ('journalctl -u SERVICE --since=-1h')?
CLARIFY: Which database? Postgres has log_min_duration_statement, MySQL has slow query log. Need to enable that and check the corresponding log file - confirm DB.
CLARIFY: Forward journald to a remote (systemd-journal-remote), use rsyslog to a syslog server, or ship with a different agent (vector, fluent-bit)? Where to?
CLARIFY: Where ufw logs to - /var/log/ufw.log (if separate logging enabled), or in /var/log/syslog. Are you looking for blocked traffic only? Confirm.
CLARIFY: Postfix? /var/log/mail.log and /var/log/mail.err. Or another MTA (exim, sendmail)? Confirm.
CLARIFY: ufw blocks go to /var/log/ufw.log (with LOGGING on). For iptables, you'd add a LOG rule. Which firewall, and is logging enabled?
CLARIFY: From /var/log/auth.log ('sudo grep sudo /var/log/auth.log') or journal ('sudo journalctl | grep sudo')? Filter by user?
CLARIFY: It already does, in /var/log/apt/history.log and term.log. What action are you looking for - installs, removes, upgrades on a date?
CLARIFY: Just installs (grep ' install ' /var/log/apt/history.log), or full history with date range? Want package names only or full lines?
CLARIFY: Which container ('docker ps -a' to list)? 'docker logs NAME' or 'docker compose logs SERVICE'. And how much - last 100 lines, follow live?
CLARIFY: Nginx already writes access.log by default. Do you need a custom format, separate log per vhost, or to disable logging for specific paths?
CLARIFY: Back up what (which folder or file), to where (which destination), and how (a one-time tar archive, a sync via rsync, or scheduled with restic/borg)?
CLARIFY: Which file (path), and from which backup source - a local archive, an external drive, a cloud backup? Tell me both.
CLARIFY: A copy of what (file or folder path), and where should the copy be placed? Also: should it preserve permissions and timestamps?
CLARIFY: Where was the data, and what happened - deleted file (try ext4-undelete/extundelete), bad disk (need ddrescue first), or accidentally overwritten? Each is a different recovery path.
CLARIFY: Save which files to where? E.g., 'tar czf ~/backup.tar.gz ~/Documents' or 'rsync -av ~/Documents/ /mnt/external/'. Tell me source and destination.
CLARIFY: Of which folder, to where, with which tool - restic, borg, rsnapshot, rsync with --link-dest? Each has different setup.
CLARIFY: Restore from which backup tool (restic, borg, timeshift, manual snapshot)? And restore which files - all of yesterday's backup, or specific files?

column2: make a backup before i upgrade
column3: CLARIFY: A simple home folder backup (tar to external), a system snapshot (Timeshift), or full system image (Clonezilla, dd)? Where is the destination?
CLARIFY: From the trash (~/.local/share/Trash/files), from a backup (which - share path/tool), or attempt undelete on the filesystem (risky, depends on FS type)?
CLARIFY: Of which folder, to where, at what time? I'll create a cron entry or systemd timer - I need source path, destination, and schedule.
CLARIFY: Which source folder, and what's the destination - a sibling folder ('cp -r SRC SRC.copy') or somewhere else?
CLARIFY: Which database name (or all with --all-databases), and where to write the dump (file path)? Also: which user with which auth?
CLARIFY: Which database name (or all with pg_dumpall), as which user (typically postgres), and where to write the dump?
CLARIFY: Which dump file (path), into which database (name), and as which user? I'll run 'mysql -u USER DB < FILE'.
CLARIFY: Was the dump made with pg_dump (plain SQL or custom) or pg_dumpall? And which DB to restore into, as which user?
CLARIFY: Which folder, to which S3 bucket, with what tool - aws-cli ('aws s3 sync'), rclone, restic with S3 backend? And are credentials configured?
CLARIFY: For backing up which folder, to which repository (local path, B2, S3, SFTP)? I'll initialize the repo - confirm location and choose a password.
CLARIFY: Where do the emails live - Thunderbird profile (~/.thunderbird), Maildir (~/Maildir), Mbox files, or via IMAP from a server? Each is backed up differently.
CLARIFY: Which external drive (lsblk to identify), and a one-time copy ('rsync -aP ~/ /mnt/external/home/') or scheduled? Confirm mount point.
CLARIFY: For which filesystem - LVM, btrfs, ZFS each have their own snapshot mechanisms. Plus interval (hourly, daily) and retention?
CLARIFY: Which folder, and do you have the Dropbox client installed and signed in (which user)? Or do you want a one-off upload via rclone?
CLARIFY: Which folder, and use which tool - rclone with a configured Google Drive remote, or the official drive sync? Is rclone already set up?
CLARIFY: Which settings - ~/.config (most apps), ~/.bashrc, /etc files? I'll archive whichever you specify. Confirm path(s).

column2: make a backup of my project
column3: CLARIFY: Which project folder (path), and to where (tar archive in ~/backups, external drive, git repo)? Tell me both.
CLARIFY: When was it deleted, on which filesystem (ext4, btrfs, NTFS), and have you written anything to that disk since? Recovery is hit-or-miss after writes.
CLARIFY: What to back up (path), to where (path or remote), with which tool (rsync, restic, tar)? I'll add a cron entry once those are clear.
CLARIFY: Which backup tool are you using, and which files/patterns to exclude (e.g., node_modules, .cache, .git)? Tools have different exclude syntax.
CLARIFY: Which tool, and which backup destination? For restic: 'restic check'. For rsync: compare with 'diff -r' or 'rsync -n'. Tell me the tool.
CLARIFY: Which destination, and recursively as root ('sudo tar czf /backup/etc.tar.gz /etc')? Confirm output path and that you want all of /etc.
CLARIFY: Which device (lsblk), to which destination (file or another device), and which tool - dd (raw bit copy, slow), ddrescue (resilient), or partclone (filesystem-aware)?
CLARIFY: From which device, and to where? Be sure the destination has enough space - confirm size with 'lsblk' and 'df -h'. What's source and destination?
CLARIFY: Which kind of snapshot (LVM, btrfs subvolume, Timeshift), and restore what - the whole subvolume, or specific files from within?
CLARIFY: Which files (give me the list or a pattern), and where to back up to? I'll use rsync or tar with appropriate filters.
CLARIFY: For which tool - enable compression (tar.gz/xz), deduplicate (restic/borg do this), or exclude noise (node_modules, caches)? Which already exists?
CLARIFY: Initialize a git repo in /etc (etckeeper does this nicely), or just for a specific config folder (e.g., ~/.config)? Which path?
CLARIFY: Which NFS server and export, mounted to which local path? Once mounted, you can rsync to it. Are the mount details set up?
CLARIFY: Which VM (libvirt, VirtualBox, VMware), running or stopped? Snapshot (live), export OVA, or just back up the disk image file ('virsh dumpxml + cp')?
CLARIFY: Which file, and what's the timestamp format you want (e.g., file.txt.20260528, file.txt.bak.2026-05-28T15:00)?

column2: back up old data and delete
column3: CLARIFY: From which folder, what's 'old' (e.g., older than 30 days), where should the archive go, and confirm: delete originals after successful archive?
CLARIFY: Modified since when (since last backup, today, a specific date)? I can use 'find PATH -newer REFERENCE' or rely on rsync's delta logic. Tell me criteria.

column2: restore a single file from backup
column3: CLARIFY: From which backup (path to archive, restic repo, etc), and which file (path inside the backup)? And restore to where?
CLARIFY: To back up which folder(s), to which repo (local /backup or remote SSH user@host:/path)? I'll init the repo and create the first archive.
CLARIFY: Which folder, with which tool (restic and borg encrypt by default - the choice of password matters)? Where to store it?
CLARIFY: For restic ('restic check --read-data'), borg ('borg check'), rsync (re-run with --dry-run --checksum), or tar (test extraction)? Which tool?
CLARIFY: To which destination, and as a single archive or two? Plus, /etc requires sudo - confirm you want both: 'sudo tar czf BACKUP.tar.gz /etc /home/$USER'.
CLARIFY: From which local path, to which remote (user@host:/path)? And one-way mirror (--delete on dest) or just additive sync? SSH keys set up?
CLARIFY: Which file, and 'save changes' - did you mean copy to a backup name (file.bak), commit to git, or actually save in an editor (Ctrl+S in the app)?
CLARIFY: Of what scope - one folder (tar), an LVM volume (lvcreate -s), a btrfs subvolume, a full Timeshift snapshot? Confirm.

column2: back up only this week's work
column3: CLARIFY: From which folder, and 'this week' meaning since which date? I'll use 'find PATH -newermt DATE' to filter. Tell me the path and start date.
CLARIFY: Source folder and backup folder paths? 'diff -r SOURCE BACKUP' or 'rsync -anc --dry-run SOURCE/ BACKUP/' will both compare. Which two paths?
CLARIFY: Which database (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB), which DB name, and where to write the dump? Also: which user/credential?
CLARIFY: From which backup source (path/tool), and overwrite existing files or restore only missing ones? Be careful - overwriting can destroy newer changes.
CLARIFY: Which files/folder are you about to delete, and where should the backup go? I'll copy them first so we can restore if needed.
CLARIFY: Use a tool like chezmoi/yadm, or a plain bare-git repo pointing at $HOME? Which dotfiles to start with (list a few paths)?

column2: copy a directory to another disk
column3: CLARIFY: Source folder and destination disk (mount point - 'lsblk' to see mounts)? I'll use 'rsync -aHAX SRC/ DEST/' to preserve permissions and ACLs.
CLARIFY: From which folder, and how to identify 'photos' - by extension (jpg, png, heic, raw), or by location (~/Pictures)? Destination?

column2: save the config so i can revert
column3: CLARIFY: Which config file or folder? Easiest is 'sudo cp FILE FILE.bak' before changing. Tell me the path.
CLARIFY: Which tool - rsync (try --inplace, increase --bwlimit), restic (more cores, smaller chunks), tar with parallel xz? Plus what's the bottleneck (CPU, I/O, network)?
CLARIFY: Which keys - SSH (~/.ssh), GPG (~/.gnupg), age, application API keys? Each lives in a different place and may need decryption.
CLARIFY: Which tar archive (path) and which folder inside it (e.g., 'home/aditya/Documents/')? I'll use 'tar xzf ARCHIVE FOLDER/'.

column2: back up with rsync excluding caches
column3: CLARIFY: Source and destination paths, and 'caches' meaning - .cache, node_modules, __pycache__? I'll add the right --exclude flags. Confirm patterns.
CLARIFY: Compress an existing folder ('tar czf ARCHIVE.tar.gz FOLDER'), or change a backup tool's compression? Which input and output?
CLARIFY: For which backup tool - I'd set retention policy (restic 'forget --keep-daily 7 --keep-weekly 4', borg --keep-...). Tell me tool and retention.
CLARIFY: From which local path, to user@host:/path? Tool: 'rsync -aP SRC/ user@host:/path/' or 'borg create user@host:repo::name SRC'? SSH key set up?
CLARIFY: Switch to deduplicating tool (restic/borg), exclude noise, or increase compression? What's your current tool and bottleneck?
CLARIFY: Back up what scope - just /home, also /etc and package list (dpkg --get-selections), entire disk image? Plus where to (external drive, network)?
CLARIFY: NetworkManager keeps them in /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/. If you backed that up, restore those files (as root) and reload NetworkManager. Was that in the backup?
CLARIFY: Which browser (Firefox ~/.mozilla, Chrome ~/.config/google-chrome, Brave, etc.), and which profile? I'll archive the profile directory.
CLARIFY: A quick backup of what to where - /etc to /backup/etc-$(date)? Or /home? Confirm the source(s) and destination.

column2: back up only files newer than
column3: CLARIFY: Newer than what date or what reference file? E.g., 'find PATH -newermt 2026-05-20' or 'find PATH -newer REFFILE'. Tell me criteria and destination.
CLARIFY: Where is 'offsite' - cloud (S3, B2), a remote SSH server you control, a NAS at another location? Tool (rclone, restic, borg)?
CLARIFY: Tape drive device path (e.g., /dev/nst0), which tool (tar, dar, mt)? Tapes need explicit positioning - which folder to write?
CLARIFY: Trigger backup how - on file change (inotifywait), git pre-commit hook, manual? And what to back up where?
CLARIFY: For which folder, and where's the previous snapshot file (-g flag)? Plus where to write the new archive? I'll use 'tar --listed-incremental'.
CLARIFY: For which backup - I can test-extract a tar ('tar tzf ARCHIVE'), run 'restic check', or actually restore to a temp dir. Which approach and which backup?
CLARIFY: Which application's settings, and what should change? Tell me the app and the value(s) to update.
CLARIFY: Which config file (give me the path), and what change? E.g., setting a value, adding a line, replacing a block?
CLARIFY: Which application or service has the broken config, and what's the symptom or error message? Share what you have and the goal state.
CLARIFY: Which config - /etc/sysctl.conf (kernel params), /etc/fstab (mounts), /etc/hosts (name resolution), a specific service? Tell me which file and which setting.
CLARIFY: Which variable and value, and what scope - just current shell ('export VAR=VAL'), your user permanently (~/.bashrc), or system-wide (/etc/environment)?
CLARIFY: Default for what - default editor (EDITOR env), default shell (chsh), default browser (xdg-settings), default printer (lpadmin -d)? Be specific.
CLARIFY: Default editor for which user, and which editor (nano, vim, code, nvim)? I'll set EDITOR / VISUAL in your shell rc - confirm shell (bash, zsh).
CLARIFY: To which timezone (e.g., America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London, UTC)? I'll run 'sudo timedatectl set-timezone TZ' - share the IANA name.
CLARIFY: Which locale (en_US.UTF-8, en_GB.UTF-8, fr_FR.UTF-8)? System-wide (via 'sudo update-locale') or just your user (~/.profile)?
CLARIFY: Which sysctl key and value (e.g., 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=1')? Just this boot ('sysctl -w') or persisted ('/etc/sysctl.d/99-custom.conf')?
CLARIFY: What's wrong - share 'sudo nginx -t' output. Common issues: server_name conflict, missing semicolon, wrong root path. Which config file (path) and error?
CLARIFY: Main config (/etc/apache2/apache2.conf) or a site (/etc/apache2/sites-available/)? And which directive needs change?
CLARIFY: Server-side (/etc/ssh/sshd_config - then reload sshd) or client-side (~/.ssh/config)? And which setting (Port, PermitRootLogin, etc.)?
CLARIFY: Which unit (full name like nginx.service), and what change? Edit via 'sudo systemctl edit UNIT' to create overrides, or modify the unit file directly?
CLARIFY: For which shell (bash uses PS1, zsh uses PROMPT). Persist in ~/.bashrc / ~/.zshrc. What should the prompt show - user, host, path, git branch?
CLARIFY: Which environment - GNOME (gsettings), KDE (lookandfeeltool), terminal (.config or prompt), VS Code? And which theme?
CLARIFY: For your shell (~/.bashrc, ~/.profile), at system boot (systemd service, /etc/rc.local on older systems), or at desktop login (~/.config/autostart)?
CLARIFY: 'sysctl vm.swappiness' - lower means use swap less (10 for SSDs, 60 default). Set permanently in /etc/sysctl.d/? What value do you want?
CLARIFY: Which command to run, at what schedule (e.g., daily at 2am, every 15 min), as which user? I'll add a crontab line - need command, schedule, user.
CLARIFY: Add a kernel parameter (e.g., 'quiet splash'), change default kernel, or default OS in dual-boot? I'd edit /etc/default/grub then 'update-grub'. Which change?
CLARIFY: Which unit name, and which field to change (ExecStart, Restart=, User=)? I'll use 'systemctl edit UNIT' to create a drop-in override.
CLARIFY: Which entry to add or change - IP and hostname? E.g., '192.168.1.10 myserver'. I'll append to /etc/hosts with sudo. Share IP and name.
CLARIFY: Which resolver are you using (systemd-resolved, NetworkManager, plain /etc/resolv.conf)? And what should the new DNS server(s) be?
CLARIFY: For console (loadkeys / /etc/default/keyboard) or X11 (localectl set-x11-keymap)? And which layout (us, gb, de, etc.)?
CLARIFY: For systemd-timesyncd (/etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf), chronyd, or ntpd? And which servers (pool.ntp.org, time.google.com, internal)?
CLARIFY: What new hostname? I'll use 'sudo hostnamectl set-hostname NAME' and update /etc/hosts. Confirm the name.
CLARIFY: Which changes - environment variables, sysctl, network settings, mounts? Each persists in a different file. Tell me what you changed.
CLARIFY: Which variables are wrong, and in which scope (just your shell, your login env, system-wide)? Share what's set ('printenv | sort') and what should change.
CLARIFY: For which shell (bash, zsh, fish), what command alias, and persisting where (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc)? E.g., alias ll='ls -lah'.
CLARIFY: User-level (~/.gitconfig, 'git config --global') or repo-level (this repo's .git/config)? Which key (user.email, core.editor) and value?
CLARIFY: Add a host entry to ~/.ssh/config? Need Host alias, HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile. Share those and I'll write it.
CLARIFY: To which browser (firefox, google-chrome, brave-browser)? I'll use 'xdg-settings set default-web-browser BROWSER.desktop' - confirm the desktop file name.
CLARIFY: For which user, soft/hard limit, and at what value (e.g., 65535)? Persist in /etc/security/limits.d/ - tell me user and limit.
CLARIFY: Add a connection, modify an existing one, or change DNS? Share which connection (nmcli connection show) and what change.
CLARIFY: Which device or share to auto-mount, where to mount it, and which options (e.g., noauto, x-systemd.automount)? Need device, mount point, fstype.
CLARIFY: Which PAM config (/etc/pam.d/sshd, common-auth, sudo) and what's the change? PAM mis-edits can lock you out - what's the goal?
CLARIFY: In which environment - GNOME (gsettings, dconf), KDE (kglobalaccel)? And which shortcut for which action? Be specific.
CLARIFY: 'sudo locale-gen LOCALE && sudo update-locale LANG=LOCALE'. Which locale (e.g., en_US.UTF-8)? Confirm and I'll run.
CLARIFY: Which value (022 default, 027 restrict-other, 077 owner-only)? I'll set in /etc/login.defs or PAM. Confirm value.
CLARIFY: For which log file(s), with what rotation policy (daily, weekly, max size), and how many to keep? I'll write /etc/logrotate.d/CUSTOM.
CLARIFY: Edit /etc/motd (static) or dynamic via /etc/update-motd.d/ scripts? And what message? Share the content.
CLARIFY: Default shell for which user, and which shell (bash, zsh, fish, dash)? I'll run 'chsh -s /usr/bin/SHELL USER' - confirm both.
CLARIFY: 'python' currently points where (run 'which python; ls -l $(which python)')? Use update-alternatives, or just alias in your shell rc?
CLARIFY: To which path? I'd stop docker, edit /etc/docker/daemon.json with 'data-root', migrate /var/lib/docker, then start. Confirm new path and that data can be moved.
CLARIFY: Which setting (theme, fonts, key bindings, power)? Use 'gsettings list-recursively' to find keys, then 'gsettings set SCHEMA KEY VALUE'. Tell me the goal.
CLARIFY: Which file (path), and what's the error - syntax (share the line) or missing values? I'll need to see the file's content or the related app's error.
CLARIFY: For which user, and which image file? For desktop user pic, it's typically /var/lib/AccountsService/icons/USER. Confirm.
CLARIFY: Which dotfiles do you want managed (~/.bashrc, ~/.vimrc, ~/.config/nvim, ~/.gitconfig)? And via plain symlinks, chezmoi, yadm, or a bare git repo?
CLARIFY: Add which directory to PATH, and where to persist - ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, /etc/profile (system-wide)? Confirm path and scope.
CLARIFY: Which package manager - apt (/etc/apt/sources.list, /etc/apt/sources.list.d/), pip (~/.pip/pip.conf), npm (~/.npmrc)? And to which mirror?
CLARIFY: Which file or folder do you want deleted? Please share the path so I don't remove the wrong thing.
CLARIFY: Fix what specifically? Share the symptom - an error message, a service that won't start, a file that won't open - and which component is involved.
CLARIFY: What's broken - a specific application, a service, the network, the GUI? Share the symptom or error you're seeing.
CLARIFY: What's currently slow on boot? Run 'systemd-analyze blame' and share the worst entries - I'll suggest disabling or fixing the heaviest ones.
CLARIFY: 'Drop caches' (sudo sysctl vm.drop_caches=3 - usually unnecessary, kernel manages this) or find/kill a memory-hungry process? Free output is what?
CLARIFY: Which process is leaking memory? Run 'ps aux --sort=-rss | head' and share the top - I'll target the right one.
CLARIFY: Top consumers ('ps aux --sort=-rss | head'), or a specific process's memory map ('pmap PID')? Which view do you want?
CLARIFY: Real-time view ('top' or 'htop'), or one-time top consumers ('ps aux --sort=-pcpu | head')?
CLARIFY: Run which command, at what specific time? I'll use 'at' (one-time) - need both the command and the time (e.g., 'now + 1 hour', '15:30 today').
CLARIFY: Which command, on which day of the week, at what time? I'll write a cron entry or systemd timer - share command + schedule.
CLARIFY: Which job - cron line ('crontab -l' to list), at-job ('atq'), or systemd timer ('systemctl list-timers')? Tell me which.
CLARIFY: For your user (crontab -l, atq, systemctl --user list-timers), system-wide (sudo crontab -l, /etc/cron.*, /etc/systemd/system/*.timer), or both?
CLARIFY: Which command - I'll write a cron entry using '* * * * 1-5'. Share the command and the time-of-day to run.
CLARIFY: All users including system accounts ('getent passwd' or 'cut -d: -f1 /etc/passwd'), or just human users (UID >= 1000)?
CLARIFY: Add your user to the sudo group ('sudo usermod -aG sudo USER'), or specific sudoers rules? Be aware - you need an existing sudo user to do this.
CLARIFY: Which user (gpasswd -d USER sudo)? And also check /etc/sudoers.d/ in case they have a custom NOPASSWD entry - which user?
CLARIFY: Daemon info ('docker info'), running containers ('docker ps'), all containers ('docker ps -a'), or images ('docker images')? Which?
CLARIFY: Which container? Run 'docker ps' to list, then I'll 'docker stop NAME'. Or do you mean stop all ('docker stop $(docker ps -q)')?
CLARIFY: Which image (run 'docker images' for names and tags)? I'll 'docker rmi IMAGE:TAG' - confirm exact reference.
CLARIFY: For docker-compose ('docker compose build SERVICE' then up), or a standalone Dockerfile (which path)? Which container and where's the Dockerfile?
CLARIFY: Which container name? I'll 'docker logs -f NAME' to follow live, or 'docker logs --tail=200 NAME' for recent history.
CLARIFY: Which container, and which shell (bash, sh, ash)? I'll 'docker exec -it NAME bash' - confirm container name.
CLARIFY: 'docker system prune' (containers, images, networks - safe), '-a' (also images without containers - more aggressive), '--volumes' (also data - destructive)?
CLARIFY: Which image and tag (e.g., nginx:1.27, postgres:16)? I'll 'docker pull IMAGE:TAG'.
CLARIFY: From which directory (where docker-compose.yml lives), and detached ('docker compose up -d') or foreground? I'll need the directory.
CLARIFY: From which directory (the one with compose file)? 'docker compose down' stops and removes containers; 'docker compose stop' only stops. Which?
CLARIFY: Which container (and was it started via plain docker run or compose)? I'll set --restart=unless-stopped via docker update or in the compose file.
CLARIFY: For which repo (or are you already in one)? Full log ('git log'), oneline ('git log --oneline'), graphical ('git log --graph --oneline --all')?
CLARIFY: Keep the changes in your working tree ('git reset --soft HEAD~1'), or discard them entirely ('git reset --hard HEAD~1' - destroys work)?
CLARIFY: To which branch (run 'git branch -a' to list)? I'll 'git checkout BRANCH' or 'git switch BRANCH'. Confirm name and that working tree is clean.
CLARIFY: What name, and from which base (current HEAD by default, or another branch)? I'll 'git checkout -b NAME [BASE]'.
CLARIFY: Which branch name, and local only ('git branch -d NAME') or also remote ('git push origin --delete NAME')? Has it been merged?
CLARIFY: Stage everything and commit? Then push? I need a commit message, and which files (all changes vs. specific ones).
CLARIFY: All uncommitted changes ('git restore .' or 'git checkout -- .'), or specific files? This destroys work - confirm which.
CLARIFY: Which file, and to which version - last commit ('git restore FILE'), a specific commit ('git checkout SHA -- FILE')?
CLARIFY: In git ('git diff' for unstaged, 'git diff --staged' for staged, 'git log -p' for committed), in the filesystem ('find PATH -mtime -1'), or in a config? Which?
CLARIFY: By what - author ('git log --author=NAME'), message text ('git log --grep=TEXT'), file changed ('git log -- PATH'), date? Which criterion?
CLARIFY: Merge which branch into your current branch, or vice versa? I'll 'git merge OTHER' from your current branch - confirm direction.
CLARIFY: From which remote and branch ('git pull origin BRANCH' or just 'git pull' if upstream is set)? Are local commits ahead, and do you prefer rebase or merge?
CLARIFY: Which remote (default origin) and branch (current)? If first push of branch, I'll add '-u origin BRANCH'. Confirm.
CLARIFY: Remote name (origin), and URL (https://... or git@...)? Run 'git remote add NAME URL' - share URL.
CLARIFY: From which URL, into which folder (default the repo name)? Also: shallow clone (--depth=1) to save space?
CLARIFY: Add what patterns to .gitignore (e.g., node_modules, .env, *.log)? Share the patterns and I'll append to the right file.
CLARIFY: All tracked changes (git stash) or including untracked ('git stash -u')? And want a message label ('git stash push -m MSG')?
CLARIFY: System config ('git config --system --list'), user config (--global --list), or this repo (--local --list)? Which scope?
CLARIFY: For just future commits (set user.name and user.email), or rewrite past commits (rebase --rewrite history - changes SHAs)? Which?
CLARIFY: For which file? I'll run 'git blame FILE' to show per-line authors. Confirm path.
CLARIFY: Via SSH ('ssh -T git@github.com') or HTTPS ('git ls-remote https://github.com/owner/repo.git')? Which protocol do you use?
CLARIFY: Generate a new SSH key (which type - ed25519 recommended)? Or configure an existing key for GitHub - I'll point to ~/.ssh/config. Confirm.
CLARIFY: All ('systemctl list-units --type=service'), only active ('--state=running'), only enabled at boot ('list-unit-files --state=enabled')?
CLARIFY: In which directory, and how recent - last hour ('find PATH -mmin -60'), last day ('-mtime -1'), since a date? Tell me the directory.
CLARIFY: In which directory, and how new (created or modified in the last hour, day, week)? I'll use find with -mtime or -mmin - tell me the path and window.
CLARIFY: Top CPU consumers ('ps aux --sort=-pcpu | head'), per-CPU breakdown ('mpstat -P ALL'), or interactive ('htop')?
CLARIFY: Drop page cache (sudo sysctl vm.drop_caches=3 - usually no point unless debugging), kill heavy process (which), or restart a leaking service?
CLARIFY: Live per-process ('sudo iotop'), per-device stats ('iostat -xz 1'), or read/write totals ('cat /proc/diskstats')? Which view?
CLARIFY: Slow how - using most CPU ('ps aux --sort=-pcpu'), most memory ('--sort=-rss'), most I/O ('iotop')? Which metric do you want?
CLARIFY: For which PID or process name? Run 'lsof -p PID' or 'lsof -c PROCNAME'. Tell me which.
CLARIFY: Run 'systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled' - which ones are unneeded for you? I'll disable+stop the ones you list.
CLARIFY: All TCP ('ss -tan'), all listening ('ss -tln'), all UDP ('ss -uan')? Plus do you want process names ('-p', needs sudo)?

column2: show me cpu usage per core
column3: CLARIFY: Live ('mpstat -P ALL 1' or 'htop' with cores enabled), or one-shot snapshot ('mpstat -P ALL')? Install sysstat if mpstat is missing.
CLARIFY: Which app (process name or PID)? I'll use 'ps -p PID' periodically, or top filtered to that PID. Confirm.

column2: see who is logged in via ssh
column3: CLARIFY: Currently ('who | grep pts' or 'ss -tnp src :22'), or historical attempts ('last -i')? Which?
CLARIFY: Which command/script should become a systemd service - I need the ExecStart command, the user to run as, and the service name. Share those.
CLARIFY: Which update broke things - apt upgrade (revert with snapshots/Timeshift), a kernel (boot previous kernel from GRUB), an application (downgrade which)? Specifics?
CLARIFY: Which package, and to which version? Run 'apt-cache madison PKG' to see available versions, then 'sudo apt install PKG=VERSION'. Confirm both.
CLARIFY: Which package should not be auto-upgraded? I'll 'sudo apt-mark hold PACKAGE' - confirm name.
CLARIFY: Which package was held? Run 'apt-mark showhold', then 'sudo apt-mark unhold PACKAGE' for the right one. Confirm.
CLARIFY: What's the symptom - kernel panic, can't find init, GRUB error, hangs on boot logo? And which kernel version? Share what you see on screen.
CLARIFY: Set a different default in GRUB (sudo grub-set-default INDEX), or just choose at boot menu? Which kernel version (uname -r for current)?
CLARIFY: 'sudo apt autoremove --purge' removes unused kernels, keeping the current and one fallback. Confirm, or want to remove specific kernel versions (list which)?

column2: see how much ram i have
column3: CLARIFY: Total + used summary ('free -h'), or detailed breakdown including buffers/cache ('cat /proc/meminfo')?
CLARIFY: Summary ('lscpu') or full per-core ('cat /proc/cpuinfo')? Either works - which would help more?
CLARIFY: For NVIDIA ('nvidia-smi'), AMD ('rocm-smi' if installed, else 'glxinfo | grep -i renderer'), or generic ('lspci -nnk | grep -i vga -A3')? Which GPU?
CLARIFY: Listed devices ('lsusb'), tree view ('lsusb -t'), or detailed for one device ('lsusb -v -s BUS:DEV')? Which detail level?
CLARIFY: General summary ('inxi -Fxz' if installed, otherwise individual: lscpu, lsmem, lsblk, lspci, lsusb)? Which component?
CLARIFY: Running kernel ('uname -r'), full system info ('uname -a'), or installed kernel packages ('dpkg -l | grep linux-image')? Which?
CLARIFY: Pretty name ('lsb_release -d' or 'cat /etc/os-release'), kernel version ('uname -a'), or systemd version ('systemctl --version')? Which?
CLARIFY: Which service unit, and from where (/etc/systemd/system/ for custom, /lib/systemd/system/ for package-provided)? Removing package-provided breaks the package.
CLARIFY: Which existing user, or create new? I'd set shell to /usr/sbin/nologin, lock password, and maybe set home. Confirm username and that they shouldn't log in interactively.
CLARIFY: What username, real name, sudo access (yes/no), and shell (bash default)? I'll 'sudo adduser USER' interactively, or share all params.
CLARIFY: In which environment - GNOME (gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.background picture-uri PATH), KDE, Xfce? And what image path?
CLARIFY: List available with 'xrandr' - which output, which resolution? Or for Wayland, use the Settings app. What's your session ($XDG_SESSION_TYPE)?
CLARIFY: Detected by 'xrandr' / 'wlr-randr'? Which port (HDMI, DP) and which GPU (nvidia, amd, intel)? Driver up to date? Share xrandr output.
CLARIFY: PulseAudio or PipeWire ('pactl info' shows)? What's the symptom - no sound, wrong device, crackling? And what device (run 'pactl list short sinks')?
CLARIFY: Which sink (run 'pactl list short sinks' for names)? I'll 'pactl set-default-sink NAME' - share the name.
CLARIFY: What's wrong - won't pair, paired but no sound, low quality? And which device. Share output of 'bluetoothctl devices' and what symptom.
CLARIFY: Add a new printer (which model, what IP/USB), set default, or fix one not working? Plus is CUPS running ('systemctl status cups')?
CLARIFY: Default printer or specific? 'lp /usr/share/cups/data/testprint' to default, or '-d PRINTER' to choose. What's the printer name ('lpstat -p')?
CLARIFY: For ufw ('sudo ufw status verbose'), firewalld ('sudo firewall-cmd --state'), or iptables ('sudo iptables -L -v -n')? Which is active?
CLARIFY: Which rule and which firewall? Run 'sudo ufw status numbered' (or firewall-cmd --list-all) and tell me the rule number or specification.
CLARIFY: For iptables ('iptables-save > /tmp/rules.v4'), nftables ('nft list ruleset > /tmp/nft.txt'), ufw (copy /etc/ufw/), firewalld (copy /etc/firewalld/)? Which?
CLARIFY: Recent log ('sudo journalctl -u ssh -n 50'), active connections ('sudo ss -tnp src :22'), config ('sudo cat /etc/ssh/sshd_config')? Which?
CLARIFY: For your user ('crontab -l'), root ('sudo crontab -l'), or all users (read /var/spool/cron/crontabs/* as root)? Which?
CLARIFY: System cron tabs ('sudo ls /etc/cron.*'), user crontabs (sudo ls /var/spool/cron/crontabs), or systemd timers ('systemctl list-timers --all')? All sources?
CLARIFY: What name (substring or exact), and where to search (your home, the whole filesystem, a specific path)?
CLARIFY: What text or phrase to search for, and in which directory tree? I'll use 'grep -r PATTERN PATH'.
CLARIFY: Live live per-process ('sudo iotop'), per-device ('iostat -x 1'), or kernel I/O stats ('cat /proc/diskstats')? Which?

column2: find what makes a sound at boot
column3: CLARIFY: Looking for boot-time audio (PulseAudio/PipeWire startup, the welcome chime)? Tell me what should be silenced - the GNOME login sound, or all desktop notifications?
CLARIFY: For what purpose - watch a meeting, remote desktop, presentation share? Tools differ (browser-based for meetings, vino/krfb for VNC desktop, x11vnc).
CLARIFY: What's wrong - draining too fast (find which process - powertop), not charging (firmware/BIOS check), or showing wrong percentage (recalibrate)? Symptoms?
CLARIFY: 'upower -i $(upower -e | grep BAT)' shows capacity, charge, state. Or use 'cat /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/charge_full*'. Confirm interest.
CLARIFY: Reduce CPU frequency (cpupower set powersave governor), lower fan curve (depends on hardware - need EC tool), or quiet a specific app? Goal?
CLARIFY: On which interface? Enable in firmware (BIOS) + 'sudo ethtool -s INTERFACE wol g' + persist via NetworkManager or a service. Share interface name.
CLARIFY: Which camera device (list with 'v4l2-ctl --list-devices' or 'ls /dev/video*')? I'll preview with 'ffplay /dev/videoN' or guvcview - which?
CLARIFY: For which user, and what counts as their data - home folder (/home/USER), mail spool, cron, plus anywhere they own outside home? Tell me the username and scope.
CLARIFY: Faster how - boot time (systemd-analyze blame), GUI responsiveness (check GPU drivers), disk speed (move to SSD), or a specific slow app?
CLARIFY: What scope - apt cache + autoremove (safe), also user caches, also old kernels, also docker prune? Each is more invasive. List which categories.

column2: find files that shouldnt be here
column3: CLARIFY: 'Shouldn't be here' meaning - duplicates, files with no owner, world-writable, unexpected setuid, very large, or very old? Each is a different scan.
CLARIFY: Journal entries ('journalctl --vacuum-time=30d') or rotated files in /var/log ('find /var/log -name "*.gz" -mtime +30 -delete')? Both?

column2: see what services start on boot
column3: CLARIFY: All enabled service units ('systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled --type=service'), or only services currently running ('systemctl list-units --type=service')?
CLARIFY: Which app, and how should it behave - run as a user systemd service, started on login via autostart, or just nohup for one session? Tell me the app and goal.
CLARIFY: Once (now + N minutes via 'sudo shutdown -r +N'), or recurring (cron @reboot is not the answer - that's at-boot). What's the schedule?
CLARIFY: If it was 'shutdown -r', cancel with 'sudo shutdown -c'. If scheduled via cron/timer, share which and I'll remove it.

column2: see when system was last started
column3: CLARIFY: Last boot time ('uptime -s') or boot history ('last reboot')? Either works.

column2: make this folder backed up regularly
column3: CLARIFY: Which folder, to where, with what tool (rsync, restic, borg), and how often (daily, hourly)? I'll set up a systemd timer or cron once those are clear.

column2: set up filesync between two computers
column3: CLARIFY: Which two hosts, which folder on each, and which tool (Syncthing - peer-to-peer, Unison - bidirectional, rsync - one-way)? Network reachable?
CLARIFY: Full disk image (clonezilla, dd - destination drive needed), file-level backup of '/' (need lots of space, exclude /proc /sys /dev), or system snapshot (Timeshift)?
CLARIFY: In /var/log ('sudo du -ah /var/log | sort -h | tail -10'), in your home, or somewhere else? Want only specific types (e.g., .log)?
CLARIFY: Just list ('cat ~/.ssh/known_hosts') or search for a specific host ('ssh-keygen -F HOST')? Or system-wide /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts?
CLARIFY: Which host's entry should I remove? 'ssh-keygen -R HOSTNAME' removes it from known_hosts. Share the hostname.
CLARIFY: For which host (hostname or IP)? I'll connect with 'ssh-keyscan' and add to known_hosts, or you can connect once and accept the prompt. Share host.
CLARIFY: What username, do they need shell access (no by default for sftp-only), and chrooted to which directory? Share those for /etc/ssh/sshd_config tuning.
CLARIFY: To which host, as which user? I'll need to copy your public key (ssh-copy-id user@host) and confirm key-only auth is desired.
CLARIFY: Which type (ed25519 recommended, rsa for older systems), and where to save (default ~/.ssh/id_ed25519)? Plus passphrase or no? Confirm.
CLARIFY: From what to what - OpenSSH to PuTTY (puttygen), PEM to PPK, public to authorized_keys format? Tell me input and target.
CLARIFY: Just your ~/.ssh folder (chmod 700 keys), or also /etc/ssh server config? Where to (encrypted archive recommended for keys)?

column2: use a different key for this host
column3: CLARIFY: For which host (alias or hostname), and which IdentityFile path? I'll add a Host block to ~/.ssh/config - share both.
CLARIFY: Start ssh-agent now ('eval $(ssh-agent)'), or auto-start with desktop (gnome-keyring usually does this). And which keys to add ('ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519')?
CLARIFY: Which key (run 'ssh-add -l' to list)? I'll 'ssh-add -d PATH'. Or remove all with 'ssh-add -D'. Confirm.
CLARIFY: User cache ('pip cache purge'), or just one package ('pip cache remove PKG')? Either is safe.
CLARIFY: 'npm cache clean --force' wipes the cache - confirm. Or only for one package? Cache rarely needs clearing - what's the symptom?
CLARIFY: 'yarn cache clean' clears all - or 'yarn cache clean PACKAGE' for one. Which?
CLARIFY: Which package, and from which environment (global pip, --user, or a virtualenv)? 'pip uninstall PACKAGE' in the active env.
CLARIFY: Which package, which version (latest by default), and where (global, --user, or active venv)? Share the package and any constraints.
CLARIFY: Where (which directory should the venv folder be in), with which Python version, and any initial packages? I'll 'python3 -m venv PATH'.
CLARIFY: Is python3 installed ('which python3')? pip can be installed with 'sudo apt install python3-pip' or 'python3 -m ensurepip'. Confirm which approach.
CLARIFY: System 'python' to point to python3 ('sudo apt install python-is-python3'), or use update-alternatives for multiple versions? Which is fine?
CLARIFY: Which Node.js major version (20 LTS, 22 current), and via which manager (nvm for per-user, n, asdf, fnm, or NodeSource apt)? Tell me both.
CLARIFY: Are you using nvm, fnm, asdf, or n? Each has different command - 'nvm use 20', 'fnm use 20', 'asdf set nodejs 20.0.0'. Which?
CLARIFY: Just one project's ('rm -rf ./node_modules'), or across many projects? If many, give me the parent directory to search under.
CLARIFY: For the current Node ('npm ls -g --depth=0'), or for a specific node version? Confirm.
CLARIFY: Which package name? I'll 'npm uninstall -g PACKAGE'. Confirm name (run 'npm ls -g --depth=0' to list).
CLARIFY: In which Go project (cd to the module first), and which package path? I'll 'go get PACKAGE'. Share the module URL.
CLARIFY: GOPATH (older modules) or GOBIN (binaries)? And to which directory? Persist in ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile - share values.
CLARIFY: Don't use sudo pip - prefer per-user install ('pip install --user PKG') or a virtualenv. Which package, and which approach do you want?
CLARIFY: For which package manager - apt ('dpkg -l'), pip ('pip list'), npm ('npm ls'), snap, flatpak? Or a specific search across them?
CLARIFY: Which command? 'apt-file search /usr/bin/COMMAND' (after apt-file update) or 'command-not-found COMMAND' (often suggests). Share the command name.
CLARIFY: 'snap list' shows installed - confirm? Or want only those needing updates ('snap refresh --list')?
CLARIFY: Which snap package? 'sudo snap remove NAME' - confirm name (run 'snap list' to see). To also purge data, add '--purge'.
CLARIFY: 'flatpak list' shows installed - confirm? Or want only apps ('flatpak list --app') and not runtimes?
CLARIFY: Which flatpak (run 'flatpak list --app' for app IDs)? 'flatpak uninstall APP_ID'. Confirm.

column2: find what is using my microphone
column3: CLARIFY: 'pactl list source-outputs' shows active capturers in PulseAudio; for PipeWire use 'pw-cli ls Node | grep -A5 capture'. Which audio system are you on?
CLARIFY: 'sudo fuser -v /dev/video0' shows processes holding the camera. Which video device do you mean (ls /dev/video*)?
CLARIFY: For which file? 'file PATH' tells you. Share the path.
CLARIFY: Which two files, and how - text diff ('diff FILE1 FILE2'), side-by-side ('diff -y'), or byte-level for binary ('cmp')?
CLARIFY: Which two folders, and detail level - names only ('diff -rq A B'), full content diff ('diff -r A B'), or rsync dry-run for sync status?
CLARIFY: Which file, and which hash (md5sum, sha1sum, sha256sum)? Share the file path and algorithm.
CLARIFY: For which file, and what's the expected checksum (or a checksum file with the manifest)? Algorithm (md5, sha256)?
CLARIFY: Which file, and with what tool (gpg, age, openssl)? gpg with a passphrase or a recipient key? Confirm tool and key/passphrase choice.
CLARIFY: Which encrypted file, and with what tool (was it gpg, age, openssl)? Do you have the passphrase or private key ready?
CLARIFY: Which file, and with which key (gpg -K to list)? Detached signature (-b) or inline? Confirm.
CLARIFY: Which signature file and which signed file? 'gpg --verify SIG FILE'. Share the paths.
CLARIFY: Public ('gpg --list-keys'), private ('gpg --list-secret-keys'), or detailed (--list-keys --with-colons)? Which?
CLARIFY: From a file ('gpg --import FILE'), from a keyserver ('gpg --keyserver SERVER --recv-keys KEYID'), or from clipboard? Share source.
CLARIFY: Public ('gpg --delete-keys KEYID') or also private ('gpg --delete-secret-keys KEYID')? And which key (run 'gpg -K' for IDs)?
CLARIFY: Cron output goes to mail by default, or to /var/log/syslog. Check 'grep CRON /var/log/syslog' or 'journalctl -u cron'. Which is more useful?

column2: run a script as another user
column3: CLARIFY: Which script, and as which user? 'sudo -u USER /path/script' - confirm user and script path.
CLARIFY: Run which command as root, with environment? 'sudo COMMAND' for one command, 'sudo -i' for a full root shell. Which?
CLARIFY: 'uptime' shows uptime + load + users. Want just boot time ('uptime -s'), or pretty ('uptime -p')?
CLARIFY: All open files system-wide ('lsof' - large output), by a specific process ('lsof -p PID'), or by file ('lsof FILE')? Which scope?

column2: see who is using a file
column3: CLARIFY: Which file? 'sudo lsof FILEPATH' shows processes holding it open. Confirm path.
CLARIFY: For which process - I can lower priority with 'renice 10 -p PID' (still uses CPU when idle), or hard cap via cgroups/cpulimit. Which?
CLARIFY: Which PID or process name? 'kill -STOP PID' pauses; 'kill -CONT PID' resumes. Confirm target.
CLARIFY: Which PID was stopped? 'kill -CONT PID' resumes. Run 'ps -ostat,pid,cmd' and look for 'T' (stopped) - share PID.
CLARIFY: Which command - I'd suggest redirecting stdout/stderr ('CMD > /dev/null 2>&1') or finding a quiet flag (-q in many tools). Share the command.

column2: make script run once a day
column3: CLARIFY: Which script (path), and which user runs it? At what time? I'll add a daily cron entry - share path, user, time.
CLARIFY: In which directory? 'find PATH -type f -size +100M -delete' is destructive - confirm path and that you want immediate delete (vs. listing first).

column2: find files i havent opened in a year
column3: CLARIFY: 'find PATH -atime +365 -type f' uses access time, which many filesystems don't update accurately. Which directory? Mtime is more reliable - which would you prefer?
CLARIFY: For which file? 'stat PATH' shows access/modify/change times - confirm the path.
CLARIFY: Which file, and to what timestamp (use 'touch -d "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" FILE' or '-r OTHER' to match another file)?
CLARIFY: Which directory, and what to do on change - just log, run a script (which)? Tool: inotifywait. Share path and trigger.
CLARIFY: Which input file (or batch), and to what format (png, jpg, webp)? I'll use 'convert INPUT OUTPUT' from ImageMagick - need both.
CLARIFY: Which file, and to which dimensions (e.g., 800x600, 50%)? Preserve aspect ratio? 'convert INPUT -resize 800x600 OUTPUT'.
CLARIFY: Which folder, which formats to include, target size, output - overwrite or new folder? Tool: ImageMagick mogrify or a script.
CLARIFY: Which input file, to which format/codec (mp4 h264, webm vp9, mkv), and any quality settings (CRF, bitrate)? Output path?
CLARIFY: Which video file, and target audio format (mp3, m4a, opus)? I'll 'ffmpeg -i INPUT -vn -acodec copy OUTPUT.m4a' or transcode - which?
CLARIFY: Which video files (paths, in order)? Same codec/container? If yes, simple concat; if no, transcode required. Output path?
CLARIFY: Which file, start and end times (e.g., 00:01:00 to 00:02:30), and output path? I'll 'ffmpeg -ss START -to END -i IN OUT'.
CLARIFY: Which PDF, and what target quality (low ~72dpi, medium ~150dpi, high ~300dpi)? I'll use Ghostscript - share input and target.
CLARIFY: Which PDFs (paths, in order), and output filename? Tool: pdfunite or pdftk - I'll use pdfunite.
CLARIFY: Which PDF, and how to split - one file per page, by page ranges (1-5,6-10), or extract specific pages? Output naming?
CLARIFY: Which input file, to what output format (docx, pdf, html, md)? Tool: pandoc for many formats, libreoffice --convert-to for office docs. Share both.
CLARIFY: 'notify-send TITLE BODY' for a desktop notification - confirm? Or send to a service (email, Slack, ntfy) - which?
CLARIFY: Which text, and which TTS engine (espeak-ng for simple, festival, or a higher-quality one like piper)? Output to speakers or save to file?
CLARIFY: From what language to what language, and which tool (trans from translate-shell, or an online API)? Plus the text or file to translate.
CLARIFY: With what - another machine (clipboard sync tool like clipnotify+xclip+netcat), another user, or save to file ('xclip -selection clipboard -o > file')?
CLARIFY: On X11 ('xclip -selection clipboard -o' or 'xsel --clipboard --output'). On Wayland ('wl-paste'). Which session ($XDG_SESSION_TYPE)?
CLARIFY: From what source - a file ('xclip -selection clipboard < FILE'), a string ('echo TEXT | xclip')? And X11 (xclip) or Wayland (wl-copy)?
CLARIFY: To what level (0-100), and via which interface - 'brightnessctl set N%' (recommended) or writing /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness? Confirm.
CLARIFY: What's wrong - stuck at full, can't lower, keys don't work? Hardware - laptop model? And which kernel? Share lspci and uname -r.
